objective: Make the branch-protection page state what the committed ruleset actually requires, and make the checker refuse a declaration whose prose contradicts it, so a documented review guarantee cannot be asserted while no artifact tests it.
decision_supported: Does the page a reader trusts describe the same review requirements that .github/rulesets/main-protection.json declares, and does a command fail when the two disagree?
acceptance: One direction is chosen and applied: the page now says the declaration requires no approving review, does not dismiss a stale approval on push and does not block on unresolved conversations, and says why.

The reason is the one the two most recent commits already recorded: one active maintainer and no reviewer who could approve, so the requirement was unsatisfiable and every merge needed a recorded administrator bypass; what reviews a change is the status matrix with administrator bypass disabled.

The checker refuses a declaration whose prose contradicts it: prose_reasons reads the page and reports a declaration that disables a guarantee the page states, for the three review guarantees the page can make.
The prose comparison runs before the live comparison, so a contradiction is caught without a token, and --prose selects the page.
check_branch_protection.py --live still works with a recorded payload, so the comparison is exercised without an admin token.
The page's table matches required_status_checks exactly and lists static-and-cpu-image separately as observed_but_not_required with the reason it does not gate a merge.
No other security document changes and .github/rulesets/main-protection.json is unchanged: this issue corrects one page and one checker, not the declaration.
A new test feeds require_pull_request false together with a documented stale-review guarantee and expects a FAIL verdict, and the same for the conversation-resolution and approval guarantees.
evidence: check_branch_protection.py before the page fix: the documented review guarantees contradict the declaration, naming dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push and require_conversation_resolution, exit code 1.
The same command after the fix: it proceeds to the live comparison and reports the legacy payload's real gaps, which is the behaviour that was intended.

pytest output for tests/unit/test_branch_protection_gate.py: 47 passed, including the three contradiction cases, the happy path, the silence case, the CLI refusal without a token and the table-versus-declaration case.
ruff check and ruff format --check output, both clean.
A full make test comparison against the unmodified main baseline showing the same pre-existing environment-blocked failures and no new ones.
stop_conditions: Applying the other direction would require editing .github/rulesets/main-protection.json to require a pull request and one approving review; the issue allows either direction but the repository cannot satisfy a review requirement today, and the declaration is read-only in this packet.
The change would have to weaken check_branch_protection.py's existing exit-code contract or treat an unobservable live configuration as a pass.
A write outside allowed_paths is required, especially to another workflow or to the ruleset declaration.
The page would have to be corrected by deleting the whole section rather than stating what the declaration requires and why.
data_classification: Repository-local Markdown, Python and a committed JSON declaration. No credentials, private data or unreviewed assets are read, written or logged.
model_policy: Deterministic Python and a local pytest run; no model inference and no network access added by this change. The live comparison is exercised through a recorded payload.
risks_and_fallbacks: The prose matcher could flag a page that quotes a guarantee in order to deny it. The patterns are written to match the asserting sentence rather than the negated form, and the page is written to state the negation plainly; a false positive is a one-line pattern change, not a gate failure that can be ignored.

The prose check could be bypassed by rewording the page so it no longer matches a pattern while still overclaiming. That is the same class of gap the issue describes, and the table-versus-declaration test covers the mechanical half; a reviewer still judges the prose.

Rollback is a revert of this commit: restore the two paragraphs and remove prose_reasons and its tests. The declaration is untouched, so nothing about enforcement changes on rollback; only the detection of the contradiction is lost.
